info.title: Mistilteinn - Genshin Optimizer
info.description: Genshin Impact build optimizer and rotation simulator

get.description: Report that the API process is up and able to serve requests.

schema.title: Response Health Check Api V1 Health Get

post.description: Register a new account. Returns pending status; no session token issued.
Authenticate with email + password. Returns session token on success.
Invalidate the current session. Requires a valid bearer token.

get.description: Return the authenticated user's profile. Accessible to PENDING and APPROVED users.
List the caller's saved teams.

post.description: Create a team of up to three builds.

get.description: Fetch a single team by id.

patch.description: Partially update a team's name or member builds.

get.description: List characters, filtered by element, weapon type, rarity or name substring.

One character with its talents, constellations and ascension passives.

The path parameter is a **string**: 28 of the 150 characters are Traveler variants
keyed `10000005-2` … `10000005-8`. Typing it as an int would 422 on all of them.
List weapons, filtered by type, rarity or name substring.
One weapon with its refinement rows and growth curves.
List artifact sets with their bonus affixes.
One artifact set with its affixes.

List enemy profiles.

The stats in each row are **curve bases**, not level-90 numbers; `stat_curves` names
the curve each one grows on. See `EnemyProfileRead`.

One enemy profile by row id.

By row id, not `nanoka_id`, because `nanoka_id` is **nullable**: a hand-authored
profile — a test dummy, a crossval target — is a legitimate row that no importer owns
and would be unreachable through a source-keyed route.
The caller's artifacts, in game slot order — flower, plume, sands, goblet, circlet.

The caller's whole inventory at one instant, for the client-side search.

Answers `304` when the caller already holds this version. See `InventorySnapshot` for
why the browser holds it at all (OQ-S3).

post.description:
Import a GOOD export into the caller's inventory.

`mode` is required — see `GoodImportRequest`. A malformed *envelope* is a 400, because
the file is not a GOOD export at all and nothing about it can be salvaged. A malformed
*artifact* is not: it lands in `rejected` and the rest of the inventory imports, because
someone with 800 artifacts and two odd ones wants the 798.

A `replace` that resolved **nothing** is a 409 and deletes nothing — see
`ReplaceRefusedError`.

get.description: One of the caller's artifacts.

delete.description:
Delete one of the caller's artifacts.

404 rather than 403 for a piece owned by someone else: the repository is scoped, so a
foreign id is indistinguishable from a missing one here — and telling a caller which of
the two it was would confirm that some other user owns that id.

get.description: The caller's saved builds, newest first.
One of the caller's builds.

patch.description: Partially update one of the caller's builds.

delete.description: Delete one of the caller's builds. Its artifacts are unequipped, not deleted.

post.description:
Search the caller's inventory for the best five pieces for this build.

**200 with the answer, or 202 with a job id.** A search that fits inside
`optimizer_job_service.SYNC_SECONDS` runs here and returns its result; a larger one is
queued and answered with a `poll_url`. A contract that always returned a job id would
make the ordinary case worse in order to serve the rare one.

schema.title: Response Optimize Build Api V1 Builds  Build Id  Optimize Post

post.description:
Rank the caller's artifacts by what each is worth *instead of* what is equipped.

Needs all five slots filled: a ranking measures a swap, and with an empty slot every
candidate for it would score as a free upgrade.

get.description:
The caller's jobs, newest first.

Summaries only: a finished job's `result` is a full optimize response, and a list of
twenty of them is a payload nobody asked for.

One job: its status, its progress, and its result once it has one.

Progress is `combinations_done` against `combinations_total`, plus the counts of what
was rejected before scoring — a search that is 90% done and rejecting almost everything
is a constraint the caller should loosen, and that is readable here while it runs rather
than only from the finished result.

post.description:
Ask a queued or running job to stop.

Cooperative: a queued job is dropped before it ever starts, and a running one stops at
its next progress tick — a couple of seconds — because a synchronous CPU-bound loop
offers no other way in. The row is marked `cancelled` by the worker as it unwinds, so a
poll immediately after this may still read `running`.

get.description:
Which ER buckets this context already has at the server's pin.

The browser asks this **first**, and simulates only the gap. A cold context answers with
an empty list rather than a 404: "nothing cached yet" is the ordinary state of a corpus
that fills on demand, and it is not an error to be in it.

post.description:
Cache a run the browser finished.

The pin is a query parameter rather than a body field so that a client which omits it
gets a 422 naming it, instead of a body validated against a default nobody chose.

get.description:
One cached run, or a 404 that says which bucket was missing.

The 404 is the outcome D.3 turns into a stated one: a caller that gets it must simulate
or say so, and must never widen its search to a neighbouring bucket and report the score
as though it were this one's.

Amplifying.title: Amplifying
Amplifying.description:
The four amplifying reactions, by *which element triggers*.

The multiplier depends on the triggering element, not on the pair. Sources, both at the
pin: `pkg/reactable/melt.go` (Pyro onto Cryo → 2.0; Cryo onto Pyro → 1.5) and
`pkg/reactable/vaporize.go` (Hydro onto Pyro → 2.0; Pyro onto Hydro → 1.5).

Transformative and additive reactions are **not** here: the BRIEF's ship order puts them
after the gauge engine, and gcsim computes them on a different path entirely
(`calcDirectReaction`, with its own `6*em/(2000+em)` bonus). Adding them to this enum
would invite them into a chain that cannot express them.

ArtifactSetRead.title: ArtifactSetRead
ArtifactSetRead.description:
One artifact set and its affixes.

`piece_thresholds` is **data**, not the constant `[2, 4]`: 60 of the 65 sets at 7.0.51
are `[2, 4]` and five are `[1]` — the "Prayers" circlets. A client hardcoding 2pc/4pc
gets those five wrong, which is why the field is on the summary and not buried.

ArtifactSlot.title: ArtifactSlot
ArtifactSlot.description:
The five artifact slots, keyed by the source's internal names.

Source: the `parts` keys of an artifact *detail* payload
(`gi/7.0.51/en/artifact/15025.json`, committed under `tests/fixtures/nanoka_gi/detail/`).

A `StrEnum` and not an `IntEnum`, per DESIGN §3: Genshin's slots are named rather than
ordered, and the fixed-main-stat property of flower and plume belongs in a
slot-to-allowed-mains table (C.5), not in the ordering of an enum.

Member names are the community/display terms; **values are the payload's keys**, which
is what the importer matches on.

AscensionPassiveRead.title: AscensionPassiveRead
AscensionPassiveRead.description:
One ascension passive.

`unlock_ascension` is **nullable and stays that way**: a passive gated by a condition
rather than a phase has no phase, and a `0` there would claim it is ungated.

CharacterRead.title: CharacterRead
CharacterRead.description: A character in full: base stats, curves, ascension table, and the kit rows.

CharacterSummary.title: CharacterSummary
CharacterSummary.description: A character as a list entry.

Element.title: Element
Element.description:
The seven visions.

Source: distinct `element` values in `gi/7.0.51/character.json` — `Anemo`, `Cryo`,
`Dendro`, `Electro`, `Geo`, `Hydro`, `Pyro`, plus a literal `"None"` carried by two
characters (the Traveler entries), which is **handled by `parse`, not mapped**.

**Physical is deliberately absent.** It is a damage type, not a vision; modelling it as
a peer of the seven is the ZZZ-shaped trap DESIGN §2.6 calls out by name. See
`DamageType`.

EnemyProfileRead.title: EnemyProfileRead
EnemyProfileRead.description:
One enemy profile.

**`base_hp` / `base_atk` / `base_def` are curve bases, not level-90 stats.** A
Hilichurl's `base_hp` is `13.584`. The number a damage calculation needs is that base
scaled by the growth curve named in `stat_curves` at `level`. Anything that multiplies
these by a crit multiplier and calls the result damage is wrong, so `stat_curves` ships
with them and the field names keep the word "base".

`level` describes what the profile is *for*; it is not a level these stats have been
evaluated at.

EnemySpec.title: EnemySpec
EnemySpec.description:
The target.

`Enemy` requires **all eight** damage channels, because treating a missing one as 0%
overstates every hit against it. Listing eight numbers on every request is not something
to ask of a caller, so any channel `resistances` does not mention takes
`default_resistance` — a **stated** default that appears in the schema and can be
changed, rather than a silent zero.

That distinction is the whole point: the first version of this documented a 10% default
and passed `{}` straight through, so every request without an explicit eight-channel map
was a 500 from inside the damage chain.

GoodImportRequest.title: GoodImportRequest
GoodImportRequest.description:
Body for `POST /artifacts/import/good`.

`mode` has **no default**, and that is the point. GOOD carries no stable per-artifact
identifier, so `append` run twice duplicates a whole inventory — and a duplicated goblet
is not clutter, it is a search that will happily recommend wearing the same piece twice.
`replace` deletes. Neither is safe to reach by omission, so the request states which.

GoodImportResponse.title: GoodImportResponse
GoodImportResponse.description:
What the import did.

`rejected` lists both the artifacts the parser refused and the ones whose set this
database does not know. A caller showing a user what happened should not have to tell
those apart, and a partial import that reported only a count would be the thing this
importer exists not to be.

HitSpec.title: HitSpec
HitSpec.description:
The hit a search or a ranking is judged on — **supplied, not derived**.

Deriving a talent's multiplier, scaling stat and damage channel from a character's
stored talent rows is the kit corpus's job (Chunk H), and this repo has no kit corpus.
Rather than parse a multiplier out of a `desc` string and present the result as though
it came from the game, the caller states the hit. `TODO(chunk-H)`: a `talent` field that
resolves this from the build's own character replaces it.

ImportRejection.title: ImportRejection
ImportRejection.description: One artifact that did not make it in, and why.

InventorySnapshot.title: InventorySnapshot
InventorySnapshot.description:
Every owned artifact in one response, plus the version that identifies it.

**OQ-S3, answered: the browser holds the inventory and revalidates it.** The transfer is
not the deciding factor — a 2,000-piece account is ~936 KB of JSON, ~234 KB gzipped, so
fetching per search and holding across searches cost about the same. What differs is
**staleness**: an inventory held across a GOOD re-import is an inventory containing
artifacts the user no longer owns, and a search over it would recommend wearing them.

So the payload carries a `version` and the route serves `304 Not Modified` against
`If-None-Match`. The browser keeps the pieces and asks a cheap question before each
search, which is the correctness of fetching at the cost of holding.

Paging is deliberately not offered here. `GET /artifacts` pages for a UI list; a search
needs the whole inventory at one instant, and four paged round-trips have no such
instant — a concurrent import shifts every offset under the reader.

JobAccepted.title: JobAccepted
JobAccepted.description:
202 body: the search was too large to answer inside the request.

Returned instead of `OptimizeResponse` when the estimated combination count exceeds what
`optimizer_job_service.SYNC_SECONDS` allows. Poll `poll_url` until `status` is terminal.

`estimated_combinations` and `sync_limit` are both here so "why did this become a job"
is answerable from the response, without reading the source or guessing at a threshold.

LoginResponse.title: LoginResponse
LoginResponse.description: Response for `POST /auth/login` — bearer token and its expiry.

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description: Response for `GET /auth/me` — the current user's identity and account status.

OptimizationJobRead.title: OptimizationJobRead
OptimizationJobRead.description: Response for a single job fetch — adds the original request and the full result payload.

OptimizationJobSummary.title: OptimizationJobSummary
OptimizationJobSummary.description: Response for job list/status-polling endpoints — progress only, without the large result.

OptimizeResponse.title: OptimizeResponse
OptimizeResponse.description: The ranked builds, and an honest account of the search that found them.

RankRequest.title: RankRequest
RankRequest.description:
Body for `POST /builds/{id}/rank-artifacts`.

One context per request here: ranking across several builds at once is real and useful
(`artifact_ranker` takes a list), but it needs a request shape that names them, and the
route is scoped to one build's id. `TODO(chunk-G.6c-multi)`.

RankResponse.title: RankResponse
RankResponse.description: Every candidate, best first, and what it is being compared against.

RankedArtifactRead.title: RankedArtifactRead
RankedArtifactRead.description: One artifact's marginal value against the build as currently equipped.

Rarity.title: Rarity
Rarity.description:
Star rating, normalised across the two encodings the source uses.

Characters carry `rank` as a `QUALITY_*` string; weapons carry it as an integer 1-5, and
weapon *detail* payloads call the same thing `rarity`. `parse` accepts all of them.

`QUALITY_ORANGE_SP` is 5-star. It is **not** a one-off: 15 of the 150 characters carry
it, against DESIGN §2.6's "Aloy-class special" reading. Whether the SP distinction
matters to anything downstream is a Chunk D question; it does not change the star count.

RegisterResponse.title: RegisterResponse
RegisterResponse.description: Response for `POST /auth/register` — always pending until email verification.

ScalingStat.title: ScalingStat
ScalingStat.description:
What a talent's multiplier scales off.

gcsim's `UseHP` / `UseDef` / `UseEM` flags (`damage.go:52-62`), as data on the hit
rather than flags on a branch: a talent that scales off HP is a *described* talent, not
a special case in the chain (DESIGN §1 A6).

SearchTransparency.title: SearchTransparency
SearchTransparency.description:
What the search skipped, and whether the answer is proven optimal.

`is_exact` is False only when the **lossy** layer fired. Pareto pruning is arithmetic —
a dominated piece cannot appear in an optimal build — so it does not appear here;
marking a losslessly-pruned search inexact would train a reader to ignore the flag on
the runs where it means something.

SimRunCoverage.title: SimRunCoverage
SimRunCoverage.description:
Which ER buckets this context already has, so a search knows what it must simulate.

Buckets rather than whole runs: the browser asks this before deciding how much work to
do, and shipping it every cached `result` to answer "how many" would make the cheap
question as expensive as the answer it is trying to avoid.

SimRunSubmit.title: SimRunSubmit
SimRunSubmit.description: One run the browser finished, offered to the cache.

TalentRead.title: TalentRead
TalentRead.description: One talent, with its per-level scaling table.

TalentScalingRead.title: TalentScalingRead
TalentScalingRead.description: One level's row of a talent's published multiplier table.

TeamUpdate.title: TeamUpdate
TeamUpdate.description: Body for `PATCH /teams/{id}` — all fields optional, partial update.

UserStatus.title: UserStatus
UserStatus.description: Admin-approval lifecycle state for a `User` account.

WeaponRead.title: WeaponRead
WeaponRead.description: A weapon in full, with its growth curves and refinement rows.

WeaponSummary.title: WeaponSummary
WeaponSummary.description:
A weapon as a list entry.

`base_atk` and `sub_stat_type` are nullable because eight rows (the `ITEM_TPS_WEAPON`
family, ids 224001-224008) publish `atk: null` and `sub: null`. They are imported
visibly rather than dropped; a client should expect to see them.

WeaponType.title: WeaponType
WeaponType.description:
The six weapon classes.

Source: `character.json` `weapon` and `weapon.json` `type`. **The two indexes disagree
on the sixth.** Characters spell the crossbow class `WEAPON_CROSSBOW` (2 characters);
weapons spell it `ITEM_TPS_WEAPON` (8 weapons) and `WEAPON_CROSSBOW` appears nowhere in
`weapon.json`. Both spellings therefore map here, via `parse`.

DESIGN §2.6 recorded only `WEAPON_CROSSBOW`, having read the character index alone.
